overall: The AG found the Task Force violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via email on October 17, found no violation in ending the September 30 listening session early, and ordered release of the violative emails within 30 days.

allegations.summary: Task Force members emailed the full body on Oct 17 with opinions on the substance of the final recommendation, allegedly deliberating outside a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Task Force acknowledges, and we find, that the Task Force violated the Open Meeting Law when, on October 17, Task Force members sent emails to the full body expressing their opinions on what should be included in the substance of the Task Force’s final recommendation and report.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Task Force ended its Sept 30 listening session early, preventing late arrivals from giving public comment.
allegations.key_passage: Nothing in the Open Meeting Law requires a public body to hold a meeting open for a certain period of time or past the conclusion of the meeting’s business.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the early end of the listening session violated late arrivals' First Amendment rights.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, allegations that an individual’s rights under the U.S. or Massachusetts constitutions have been violated fall outside of the Division’s statutory review.

remedy: Within 30 days, release to the public the October 17 emails containing the improper deliberation; since the Task Force has disbanded, it may post them to the municipal website.
remedy_passage: We order the Task Force, within 30 days of the date of this letter, to release to the public the October 17 emails containing the improper deliberation.
